title: Key Vault use — spoken follow-up
situation: In a technical discussion, a teammate suggests copying a sensitive value into configuration. You must answer aloud accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Say aloud why the sensitive value is not copied into configuration, and name what a reviewer would see if it were.

vocabulary.meaning: a setting whose value must never appear in source control, logs, or a support export
the full set of places a value reaches once it is stored somewhere, usually wider than the place it was written to

expectedElements: The storage location is named precisely
The exposure surface of the wrong choice is described
What a reviewer can still see is stated honestly
modelAnswer: I would not copy that value into configuration. Configuration reaches further than people expect: it lands in source control, in build logs, in a support export, and in any error page that dumps settings. The value belongs in a secret store, and the application reads it at startup through an identity rather than holding a copy. The evidence is the diff in which the setting holds a reference and not a value. The limitation is that once the application has read it, the value is in process memory, so a memory dump is still an exposure. That is a smaller surface, not no surface. Do we have a policy on dump collection?
commonMistakes: Refusing the shortcut without naming where configuration actually travels
Presenting a secret store as removing every exposure rather than narrowing it
variants: Answer again when the teammate replies that the repository is private.
